page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-192GB is a memory-dense virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on AMD EPYC 7542 processors clocked at 2.0 GHz across 16 shared vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The instance provides 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated allocation of 12.0 GB per core. The architecture supports basic x86_64 vector instructions including AVX, alongside hardware acceleration for AES and SHA extensions, but does not feature AVX-512 or AMX extensions. Local storage is not included, and the server does not contain dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier multi-threaded processing power, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 23,491.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,441.0. Geekbench single-core performance reached 2,094.0, placing in the top quartile, whereas stress-ng single-core tests scored lower at 746.4. Memory bandwidth reaches 102.97 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 74.72 GB/sec for uncached writes, while the overall PassMark memory score scored in the bottom 25% at 1,412.21. In-memory data handling remains steady, with Redis SET operations achieving 17.45 million operations per second and static web throughput reaching 11.36 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds fall off significantly on text generation, scoring in the bottom percentiles for both small and medium models.

With its 12:1 memory-to-core ratio, the platform offers qualitative cost efficiency for systems constrained primarily by RAM capacity rather than raw compute speed or GPU requirements. Shared CPU cores introduce potential contention tradeoffs compared to dedicated-core tiers. Consequently, this server is suitable for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, memory-heavy ETL processing, and backend microservices that do not rely on local NVMe disk arrays.
